items.title: Police shot Mississauga man four times during botched arrest, inquest begins
items.summary: A coroner’s inquest is set to begin today to examine the circumstances surrounding the death of a man who was shot in the head by police west of Toronto nearly seven years ago. Jamal Francique died in hospital on Jan. 9, 2020, two days after police shot him during a botched arrest in Mississauga, Ont. He was 28. About a year later, Ontario’s police watchdog cleared the Peel regional police officers of wrongdoing, saying the officer who opened fire reported fearing for his life when Francique drove at him. The Special Investigations Unit said there were aspects of the officer’s behaviour that gave rise to questions, however, such as the decision to place himself in the vicinity of a fleeing driver. The SIU said police were investigating Francique for allegedly dealing drugs and possessing a firearm at the time, but couldn’t confirm those allegations so they decided to arrest him for allegedly breaching bail conditions. The agency said plainclothes officers in unmarked cars waited for Francique to get into his car outside his home. , an officer was late blocking him in the driveway, and a second unmarked car came up behind to try to hem him in, the SIU said. Other officers got out of their cars and rushed to the area, pointing their guns at Francique, who then sped up toward a grassy area, it said.

items.title: Walmart-Backed Holiday Drive Aims to Support Mississauga Food Banks Through Jan. 8
items.summary: Food Banks Mississauga has launched its 2026 Holiday Drive, sponsored by Walmart Canada, according to The Pointer. The outlet reported the campaign runs until Jan. 8, with donations supporting the organization's network of more than 60 food programs across the city. The Pointer said demand for the organization's support has grown sharply over the past six years, as food insecurity continues to affect thousands of Mississauga residents, including a growing number of children and people with disabilities. According to the organization's recently released Annual Impact Report, one in 10 children in Mississauga relied on food banks last year. The report also found that 32 percent of food bank visitors identified as having a disability, The Pointer said. Rising costs for basic food items have made the holiday season harder for many local families, according to the report.

items.title: Mississauga Seeks Volunteer Rink-Keepers Ahead of Nov. 15 Deadline for Natural Ice Rinks
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, officials are making a last-minute push to find volunteer rink-keepers for this winter's natural ice rinks program. The city said dozens of helpers are needed to create and maintain outdoor ice surfaces at parks across the city so residents can skate or play pickup hockey. Interested applicants must sign up by Nov. 15, according to the city. Volunteers must be at least 14 and willing to work outdoors in cold temperatures, often in the late evening, the city said. Mississauga provides equipment and support for the rinks, officials noted, while volunteers handle maintenance. The rinks, including the one at Celebration Square downtown, are usually ready for skaters by late December or January once it gets cold enough, the city said. Officials described natural ice rinks as a longstanding winter tradition in Mississauga and across Canada.

items.title: Peel Region's Share, Reuse, Repair Hub Lets Residents Borrow GoPros, Telescopes and Musical Instruments for Free
items.summary: According to insauga.com, residents across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon can borrow unusual items for free through the Share, Reuse, Repair Hub, a digital resource connecting people to local lending programs. The outlet reported the hub encourages sharing, repairing, swapping or borrowing instead of buying new, as part of a push toward a more affordable, sustainable local economy. Sports equipment is among the items available, with insauga.com noting 60 equipment lockers across Peel Region stocked with soccer balls and basketballs. Libraries also lend musical instruments such as guitars, ukuleles and keyboards, the report said. Photography fans can borrow GoPro cameras for action shots during sports or travel, according to insauga.com. Stargazers can check out telescope kits with a bag and guide, the outlet noted. Availability varies by location, insauga.com said.

items.title: Adamson Estate Exhibit Tracing 70 Years of Mississauga Music Closes Dec. 27
items.summary: According to insauga.com, an exhibition on Mississauga's musical history enters its final weeks at the historic Adamson Estate before closing Dec. 27. The outlet reported the exhibition, A City in Tune: Mississauga's Greatest Hits, is presented by the Museums of Mississauga and spans nearly 70 years of the city's music scene. Featured artists include Triumph, jazz legend Oscar Peterson, Ronnie Hawkins and Billy Talent, insauga.com said. Visitors can see an autographed guitar belonging to Triumph's Rik Emmett and a drum kit tied to Gil Moore, according to the report. The exhibit also displays Donna Grantis' guitar and tour outfits, along with Billy Talent memorabilia, the outlet noted. Portraits, archival materials and a venue map round out the display, insauga.com reported. The exhibit aims to highlight figures who helped build the city's music reputation, the report said.

items.title: Canada Post to Phase Out Door-to-Door Mail Delivery in Mississauga Starting 2027
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Canada Post will begin switching thousands of Mississauga households from door-to-door mail delivery to community mailboxes starting in 2027. The outlet reported the move is part of a nationwide plan to convert about four million addresses still receiving mail at the door, with the Crown corporation aiming to finish within five years. Mississauga's rollout will run in four conversion periods from October 2027 to November 2028, organized by the first three characters of each postal code, the report said. The first neighbourhoods affected will be those with postal codes beginning with L5M and L5N, set to convert in October 2027, according to insauga.com. Residents can use that postal-code schedule to estimate roughly when their own delivery will end, the outlet noted.

items.title: Ontario's Ban on Speed Cameras Marks One Year Since Mississauga's 22 Devices Went Dark
items.summary: According to insauga.com, it has been one year since Mississauga's automated speed-enforcement cameras last captured images of speeding drivers on city roads. The outlet reported the city's 22 roadside cameras took their final photos on Nov. 13, 2025, before Ontario's ban on the devices took effect province-wide the next day. Mississauga and other municipalities opposed the ban, arguing the cameras had helped cut serious and fatal collisions, insauga.com said. Premier Doug Ford had called the cameras a cash grab, the report noted. The ban, enacted under the province's Bill 56, eliminated more than 700 speed-enforcement devices operating in 40 municipalities since 2019. Mississauga's commissioner of transportation and works, Sam Rogers, said losing the cameras would add pressure on the city's road-safety initiatives, according to insauga.com.
